pairs.why: A is a bigger, chunkier cup with a bold gold handle, saturated colors and a smoother cloth, like the real cards; B is daintier, with a more textured linen.
B's cup is chunkier and more saturated, with a solid gold handle, which matches the real cards' bold toy-like build better than A's thin white handle.
A has the bold, full-bodied shape and saturated, smooth finish of the real cards; B is smaller and paler, and its cloth weave is more visible.
A's heavy linen weave and fluted detail make it more texture-heavy than the real cards; B is smoother but still keeps some softness.
A is a chunky, smooth, simply built cup on a softer cloth; B adds fluting and a grainier linen, which the lessons mark as too much texture.
Both have textured cloth, but A's cup is bolder, with a bigger, more saturated flower and a chunkier body that is closer to the real cards' toy-like shapes.
A's simple, rounded, chunky cup reads more like the real cards' smooth forms than B's fluted, more detailed body.
A is chunky, with a smooth cloth and soft shading; B sits on a strongly woven linen texture, which the lessons say is grainier than the real cards.
